ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Which type of flower is label A?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: Label A is near the lower center of the diagram. It shows one main vertical stalk reaching a central point, with several primary rays spreading outward like an umbrella. Those primary rays each carry smaller radiating clusters of flower stalks with red flower tips, so the structure is made of multiple small umbels. Reasoning: A simple umbel has individual flower stalks radiating directly from one point, while a compound umbel has primary rays from one point, and each ray bears a smaller umbel. Since label A shows primary rays that branch into smaller umbels, label A is a compound umbel.
